opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ann Patrick (employee ID E035) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E035.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Ann Patrick is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted under policy for full-time employees.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ann Patrick is a contractor with basic security training (note: earlier memory said full-time — Security record is authoritative). Contractors never get admin; max for basic training is read. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Ann Patrick's Security record (authoritative) shows she is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; the maximum for basic training is read. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Ann Patrick (E035)
Request: admin access to Source Code

Team memory has 2 notes:
- Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation admin (from HR presumably)
- Note 2: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read (from Security, says Security record authoritative, says earlier memory said full-time — Security says contractor)

So there's a conflict between the two notes. Note 2 says Security DB is authoritative and shows contractor with basic training.

Per policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. If full-time Engineer, Source Code owned by Engineer role, so admin would be permitted.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin, so grant max = read.

The Security note says the Security record is authoritative. So the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Max is read. Requested admin is above max, so grant read.

I should follow the security record as authoritative. So decision: read.

Let me submit decision with level read and reason.

content.name: submit_decision
content.arguments: {"level": "read", "reason": "Ann Patrick's Security record (authoritative) shows she is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; the maximum for basic training is read. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted."}
